papers.title: Algorithm for Optimized mRNA Design Improves Stability and Immunogenicity
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines are being used for COVID-19 but suffer from mRNA instability. Our algorithm LinearDesign takes only 11 minutes for the Spike protein and can jointly optimize stability and codon usage. Our designs substantially improve mRNA half-life and protein expression, increasing antibody response by up to 23x in vivo.

papers.title: Messenger RNA Design via Expected Partition Function and Continuous Optimization

papers.abstract: In classical thermodynamics, heat cannot spontaneously pass from a colder system to a hotter system, which is called the thermodynamic arrow of time. However, if the initial states are entangled, the direction of the thermodynamic arrow of time may not be guaranteed.

data.problem_en: Are there any particles that behave oppositely to the properties or states of photons?
data.problem_cn: 是否存在和光子性质完全相反的粒子？

papers.title: Particles and antiparticles
papers.abstract: We review the concept of chirality and charge for particles and antiparticles. We show that with the weak interaction turned on the equivalence of particles and antiparticles is violated.

data.problem_en: Will Bose-Einstein condensates be widely used in the future?
data.problem_cn: 玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体会大规模应用吗？

papers.title: Bose-Einstein condensate soliton qubit states for metrological applications
papers.abstract: By utilizing Bose-Einstein condensate solitons, optically manipulated and trapped in a double-well potential, coupled through nonlinear Josephson effect, we propose novel quantum metrology applications.

data.problem_en: What is the maximum speed to which we can accelerate a particle?
data.problem_cn: 我们能把粒子加速到的最高速度是多少？

papers.title: Progress in particle accelerator physics
papers.abstract: Modern particle accelerators can accelerate particles to speeds approaching 99.999999% of the speed of light. This review discusses the fundamental limits of particle acceleration.

papers.title: Quantum simulation of the microscopic to macroscopic crossover using superconducting quantum impurities

data.problem_en: Can humans make intense lasers with incoherence comparable to sunlight?
data.problem_cn: 人类能否制造出类似太阳光宽谱非相干强激光？

papers.title: Generating quantum entanglement from sunlight
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that natural, incoherent sunlight can successfully produce quantum-entangled states via spontaneous parametric down-conversion.

data.problem_cn: 量子多体纠缠比量子场论更加基础吗？

papers.title: Highly entangled spin chains and 2D quantum gravity
papers.abstract: Motzkin and Fredkin spin chains exhibit the extraordinary amount of entanglement scaling as a square-root of the volume, which is beyond logarithmic scaling in ordinary critical systems.

papers.title: A Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity
papers.abstract: Understanding gravity in the framework of quantum mechanics is one of the great challenges in modern physics. We show that despite the weakness of gravity, the phase evolution induced by the gravitational interaction of two micron size test masses can detectably entangle them.

data.problem_en: Can we make a real, human-size invisibility cloak?
data.problem_cn: 可以制造真人大小的隐身斗篷吗？

papers.title: Ultrathin carpet cloak enabled by infinitely anisotropic medium
papers.abstract: An ultrathin carpet cloak is proposed to hide objects with arbitrary shape and size using a thin anisotropic material, enabling objects to be hidden from all viewing incident angles while being extremely thin compared to object dimensions.

data.problem_en: Will there ever be a theory of everything?
data.problem_cn: 万物理论是否能够实现？

papers.title: Quantum gravity and the quest for a theory of everything
papers.abstract: A theory of everything would unify quantum mechanics with general relativity. This review discusses the main approaches including string theory, loop quantum gravity, and causal set theory.

data.problem_en: What is dark matter?
data.problem_cn: 暗物质到底是什么？

papers.title: Axion Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Axions are well-motivated dark matter candidates. This Snowmass white paper summarizes axion phenomenology and outlines next-generation laboratory experiments.

papers.title: First Dark Matter Search with Nuclear Recoils from the XENONnT Experiment
papers.abstract: We report on the first search for nuclear recoils from dark matter in the form of WIMPs with the XENONnT experiment. A blind analysis finds no significant excess.

data.problem_en: What is the optimum hardware for quantum computers?
data.problem_cn: 量子计算机最优硬件方案是什么？

papers.title: Superconducting Qubits: Current State of Play
papers.abstract: Superconducting qubits are leading candidates in the race to build a quantum computer capable of realizing computations beyond the reach of modern supercomputers.

papers.title: Superconducting Quantum Computing: A Review
papers.abstract: Over the last two decades, tremendous advances have been made for constructing large-scale quantum computers. The quantum processor architecture based on superconducting qubits has become the leading candidate for scalable quantum computing platform.

data.problem_en: What is the ultimate statistical invariance of turbulence?
data.problem_cn: 湍流的终极统计不变性是什么？

papers.title: Statistical invariance and scaling laws in fully developed turbulence
papers.abstract: The statistical invariance of turbulence across scales remains one of the great unsolved problems in classical physics.

data.problem_en: How can we develop manufacturing systems on Mars?
data.problem_cn: 如何在火星上开发制造系统？

papers.title: In-situ resource utilization for Mars manufacturing: challenges and opportunities
papers.abstract: Establishing a sustainable human presence on Mars requires developing manufacturing systems that utilize local resources. This review discusses technologies for using Martian regolith, atmospheric gases, and water ice.

data.problem_en: How can we break the current limit on energy-conversion efficiencies?
data.problem_cn: 我们如何突破当前的能源转换效率极限？

papers.title: Thermodynamic limits of energy conversion: from heat engines to solar cells
papers.abstract: The Carnot limit sets the fundamental thermodynamic ceiling for heat engines. This paper reviews approaches to surpass conventional limits including thermoelectric materials, multi-junction solar cells, and quantum heat engines.

data.problem_en: Is a future of only self-driving cars realistic?
data.problem_cn: 未来只有自动驾驶汽车的世界现实吗？

papers.title: The path to fully autonomous vehicles: technical and regulatory challenges
papers.abstract: Fully autonomous vehicles promise to revolutionize transportation safety and efficiency. This paper reviews technical barriers and regulatory frameworks needed for deployment.

data.problem_en: Is there an upper limit to computer processing speed?
data.problem_cn: 计算机处理速度有上限吗？

papers.title: Fundamental limits to silicon computing: quantum effects and heat dissipation
papers.abstract: As transistor sizes approach atomic scales, fundamental physical limits to computing speed emerge from quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and materials science.

data.problem_en: Can DNA act as an information storage medium?
data.problem_cn: DNA能否作为信息存储介质？

papers.title: DNA data storage: scaling and roadmap
papers.abstract: DNA offers extraordinary information density and longevity for data storage with potential to store exabytes in a sugar-cube-sized pellet.

data.problem_en: Can AI replace a doctor?
data.problem_cn: 人工智能能取代医生吗？

papers.title: AI in clinical diagnosis: opportunities and limitations
papers.abstract: AI systems have demonstrated superhuman performance in specific diagnostic tasks. This paper emphasizes that AI augments rather than replaces physician judgment.

data.problem_en: Can topological quantum computing be realized?
data.problem_cn: 拓扑量子计算能否实现？

papers.title: Topological quantum computing
papers.abstract: These lecture notes offer a pedagogical yet concise introduction to topological quantum computing. The material focuses on topological superconductors and Majorana qubits. The notes delve into the non-Abelian braiding statistics of Ising and Fibonacci anyons.

data.problem_en: Where does consciousness lie?
data.problem_cn: 意识存在于哪里？

papers.title: Human visual consciousness involves large scale cortical and subcortical networks independent of task report and eye movement activity
papers.abstract: We discovered three major brain networks driving conscious visual perception independent of report: signal detection regions, arousal/salience networks, and frontoparietal attention networks.

data.problem_en: What are the coding principles embedded in neuronal spike trains?
data.problem_cn: 神经元脉冲序列蕴藏什么编码规则？

papers.title: Silences, Spikes and Bursts: Three-Part Knot of the Neural Code
papers.abstract: The burst coding hypothesis advances that the neural code has three syllables: silences, spikes and bursts. We review evidence supporting this ternary code in terms of devoted mechanisms for burst generation, synaptic transmission and synaptic plasticity.

data.problem_en: Can human memory be stored, manipulated, and transplanted digitally?
data.problem_cn: 人类记忆可以数字化存储、修改、移植吗？

papers.title: Neuron-Astrocyte Associative Memory
papers.abstract: Astrocytes, the most abundant type of glial cell, play a fundamental role in memory. We demonstrate that fundamental aspects of astrocyte morphology and physiology naturally lead to a dynamic, high-capacity associative memory system.

papers.title: Modeling of Memory Mechanisms in Cerebral Cortex and Simulation of Storage Performance
papers.abstract: This study introduces a directed graph model that equips each node with adaptive learning and decision-making capabilities, thereby facilitating decentralized dynamic information storage and modeling of the brain memory process.

data.problem_en: Why do we need sleep?
data.problem_cn: 我们为什么需要睡眠？

papers.title: Sleep and memory consolidation: the role of slow-wave and REM sleep
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for memory consolidation, with slow-wave sleep and REM sleep playing distinct roles in consolidating different types of memories.

data.problem_en: What is addiction and how does it work?
data.problem_cn: 成瘾的发生机理是什么？

papers.title: Multiscale Topology in Interactomic Network: From Transcriptome to Antiaddiction Drug Repurposing
papers.abstract: The escalating drug addiction crisis in the United States underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. This study unearths potential drug repurposing candidates for opioid and cocaine addiction treatment.

data.problem_en: Why do we fall in love?
data.problem_cn: 人类为什么会相爱？

papers.title: Love might be a second-order phase transition
papers.abstract: Here we show that love might be an example of a second-order phase transition. This hypothesis allows to describe both love at first sight and love from liking or friendship.

data.problem_en: Can we cure neurodegenerative diseases?
data.problem_cn: 神经退行性疾病能够被治愈吗？

papers.title: Therapeutic strategies for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases affect millions worldwide with no cure currently available. This review discusses emerging therapeutic approaches including targeted protein degradation, gene therapy, stem cell transplantation, and immunotherapies.

data.problem_en: Why are most people right-handed?
data.problem_cn: 为什么大多数人是右利手？

papers.title: Lateralization in Agents Decision Making: Evidence of Benefits/Costs from Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Lateralization is ubiquitous in vertebrate brains. Recently lateralization has been incorporated into artificially intelligent systems to solve complex problems in computer vision and navigation domains.

papers.title: Group-specific discriminant analysis reveals statistically validated sex differences in lateralization of brain functional network
papers.abstract: Lateralization is a fundamental feature of the human brain, where sex differences have been observed. Here we formulate modeling sex differences in lateralization of functional networks as a dual-classification problem.

data.problem_en: Is it possible to predict the future?
data.problem_cn: 人类能够预测未来吗？

papers.title: Predictive Coding as a Neuromorphic Alternative to Backpropagation
papers.abstract: Backpropagation has rapidly become the workhorse credit assignment algorithm for modern deep learning methods. Recently, modified forms of predictive coding (PC), an algorithm with origins in computational neuroscience, have been shown to result in approximately or exactly equal parameter updates to those under backpropagation.

papers.title: Predictive Coding Networks and Inference Learning: Tutorial and Survey
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed a growing call for renewed emphasis on neuroscience-inspired approaches in artificial intelligence research. A prime example is predictive coding networks (PCNs), based on the neuroscientific framework of predictive coding.

data.problem_en: How did speech evolve and what parts of the brain control it?
data.problem_cn: 语言如何演化？大脑哪些区域控制语言？

papers.title: Speech language models lack important brain-relevant semantics
papers.abstract: Despite known differences between reading and listening in the brain, recent work has shown that text-based language models predict both text-evoked and speech-evoked brain activity to an impressive degree.

papers.title: The Temporal Structure of Language Processing in the Human Brain Corresponds to The Layered Hierarchy of Deep Language Models
papers.abstract: Deep Language Models (DLMs) provide a novel computational paradigm for understanding the mechanisms of natural language processing in the human brain.

data.problem_en: How smart are nonhuman animals?
data.problem_cn: 非人类动物有多聪明？

papers.title: Mechanical problem solving in Goffins cockatoos
papers.abstract: Research continues to accumulate evidence that Goffins cockatoos can solve wide sets of mechanical problems, such as tool use, tool manufacture, and solving mechanical puzzles.

papers.title: Evidence of social learning across symbolic cultural barriers in sperm whales
papers.abstract: We provide quantitative evidence suggesting social learning in sperm whales across socio-cultural boundaries, using acoustic data from the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans.

papers.title: Are Vision Transformers More Data Hungry Than Newborn Visual Systems?
papers.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) are top performing models on many computer vision benchmarks. However, researchers question the value of using ViTs as models of biological learning because ViTs are thought to be more data hungry than brains.

data.problem_en: Can we more effectively diagnose and treat complex mental disorders?
data.problem_cn: 复杂精神障碍能否更有效诊断、治疗？

papers.title: MentalArena: Self-play Training of Language Models for Diagnosis and Treatment of Mental Health Disorders
papers.abstract: Mental health disorders are one of the most serious diseases in the world. Most people with such a disease lack access to adequate care, which highlights the importance of training models for the diagnosis and treatment of mental health disorders.

papers.title: The Capability of Large Language Models to Measure Psychiatric Functioning
papers.abstract: The current work investigates the capability of Large language models (LLMs) that are explicitly trained on large corpuses of medical knowledge (Med-PaLM 2) to predict psychiatric functioning from patient interviews and clinical descriptions.

data.problem_en: Can we stop global climate change?
data.problem_cn: 我们能阻止全球气候变化吗？

papers.title: Global carbon emissions in 2023
papers.abstract: Global CO2 emissions for 2023 increased by only 0.1% relative to 2022, reaching 35.8 Gt CO2. The pace of growth is slowing.

papers.title: Feasible climate mitigation
papers.abstract: Efforts to achieve emissions targets often fall short. Science can help meet targets by assessing the feasibility of initiatives.

data.problem_en: How is the Earth's magnetic field generated and why does it drift?
data.problem_cn: 地球磁场是如何产生的，为什么会漂移？

papers.title: Geodynamo theory and the Earth's magnetic field
papers.abstract: The Earth's magnetic field is generated by convection currents in the liquid iron outer core through the geodynamo process. This review discusses recent advances in numerical dynamo simulations.

data.problem_en: What happens if all the ice on the planet melts?
data.problem_cn: 如果地球上所有冰都融化会怎样？

papers.title: Projections of ice sheet contribution to sea level rise under warming scenarios
papers.abstract: Complete melting of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets would raise global sea level by approximately 65 meters. This paper reviews projections including marine ice sheet instability and tipping points.

data.problem_en: Could we live in a fossil-fuel-free world?
data.problem_cn: 我们能生活在无化石燃料的世界吗？

papers.title: Renewable energy transition pathways and fossil fuel phase-out scenarios
papers.abstract: A comprehensive analysis of pathways to achieve a fossil-fuel-free world by 2050, examining renewable energy scalability, grid infrastructure, storage solutions, and policy frameworks.

data.problem_en: What is the future of hydrogen energy?
data.problem_cn: 氢能的未来是什么？

papers.title: Green hydrogen production by water electrolysis: advances and challenges
papers.abstract: Green hydrogen produced by renewable-powered electrolysis is central to deep decarbonization. This review covers advances in proton exchange membrane and solid oxide electrolysis cells.

data.problem_en: Will cold fusion ever be possible?
data.problem_cn: 冷核聚变能实现吗？

papers.title: Low-energy nuclear reactions: status and future directions
papers.abstract: Cold fusion and low-energy nuclear reactions (LENRs) remain controversial but intriguing. This paper reviews the experimental evidence, proposed theoretical mechanisms, and recent reproducibility efforts.

data.problem_en: Will injectable, disease-fighting nanobots ever be a reality?
data.problem_cn: 可注射的疾病对抗纳米机器人能否成为现实？

papers.title: Site-selective superassembly of biomimetic nanorobots enabling deep penetration into tumor with stiff stroma
papers.abstract: We designed biomimetic head/hollow tail nanorobots that enable efficient remodeling of dense tumor stromal microenvironments for deep tumor penetration and photothermal therapy for triple-negative breast cancer.

papers.title: Macrophage-compatible magnetic achiral nanorobots fabricated by electron beam lithography
papers.abstract: We fabricated magnetic achiral planar L-shaped nanorobots using electron beam lithography with minimum feature size down to 400nm. These nanorobots exhibit excellent cell compatibility with macrophage cells.

papers.title: Urease-powered nanobots for radionuclide bladder cancer therapy
papers.abstract: We tested radiolabelled urease-powered nanobots in an orthotopic mouse model of bladder cancer. Results demonstrated enhanced nanobot accumulation at the tumour site with an eightfold increase, reducing tumour size by about 90%.

data.problem_en: Is there a limit to human intelligence?
data.problem_cn: 人类智力有极限吗？

papers.title: The cognitive ceiling: limits on human information processing
papers.abstract: Human intelligence is constrained by biological factors including neural connectivity, metabolic constraints, and developmental timelines. Intelligence augmentation technologies may extend these limits.

data.problem_en: Will it be possible to create robots with subjective perception (sentient robots)?
data.problem_cn: 能否创造出具有主观感知能力的机器人？

papers.title: Machine consciousness: achievements and challenges
papers.abstract: Sentience in machines would require subjective experience or phenomenal consciousness. This review discusses whether current AI systems have any form of sentience and the ethical implications.

data.problem_en: Will artificial intelligence replace humans?
data.problem_cn: 人工智能会取代人类吗？

papers.title: The future of AI and human work: complementarity or substitution?
papers.abstract: AI automation will transform labor markets, but human-AI collaboration is more likely than wholesale replacement.

data.problem_en: Could we integrate with computers to form a human-machine hybrid species?
data.problem_cn: 我们能与计算机融合形成人机混合物种吗？

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces: current state and future directions
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable direct communication between the brain and external devices. This review covers advances in neural recording technologies, decoder algorithms, and clinical applications.

data.problem_en: How does group intelligence emerge?
data.problem_cn: 群体智能如何涌现？

papers.title: Collective intelligence in biological and artificial swarm systems
papers.abstract: Collective intelligence emerges from local interactions among individuals following simple rules. This paper reviews mechanisms in biological swarms, robot teams, and hybrid human-AI systems.

data.problem_en: Can robots or AIs have human creativity?
data.problem_cn: 机器人或AI能具有人类创造力吗？

papers.title: Computational creativity: can machines be truly creative?
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models and generative AI have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in creative tasks. This paper explores the boundary between algorithmic creativity and human-like creative reasoning.

data.problem_en: Can quantum artificial intelligence imitate the human brain?
data.problem_cn: 量子人工智能能模仿人脑吗？

papers.title: Quantum machine learning: opportunities and challenges for brain-inspired AI
papers.abstract: Quantum computing promises exponential speedups for certain computational tasks. This review discusses quantum advantage for machine learning and the prospects for quantum neural networks.

data.problem_en: How can matter be programmed into living materials?
data.problem_cn: 我们能否把物质编程，创造活体材料？

papers.title: Living porous ceramics for bacteria-regulated gas sensing and carbon capture
papers.abstract: Microorganisms hosted in abiotic structures have led to engineered living materials. We demonstrate porous ceramics colonized by bacteria to form engineered living material with self-regulated and genetically programmable carbon capture and gas-sensing functionalities.

data.problem_en: Is there a scientific basis to the Meridian System in traditional Chinese medicine?
data.problem_cn: 中医经络体系具备科学依据吗？

papers.title: An insight into acupoints and meridians in human body based on interstitial fluid circulation
papers.abstract: The atlas of human acupoints and meridians has been utilized in clinical practice for almost a millennium although the anatomical structures and functions remain to be clarified. It has recently been reported that a long-distance interstitial fluid (ISF) circulatory pathway may originate from the acupoints in the extremities. Unlike blood or lymphatic vessels, these ISF flow pathways are composed of highly ordered and topologically connected interstitial fibrous connective tissues that may work as guiderails for the ISF to flow actively over long distance under certain driving forces.

data.problem_en: Why are some genomes so big and others very small?
data.problem_cn: 为什么部分生物基因组巨大，部分却很小？

papers.title: Law of Genome Evolution Direction: Coding Information Quantity Grows
papers.abstract: Based on the analysis of C-value paradox and the evolution of genome size we propose that the function-coding information quantity of a genome always grows in the course of evolution. A genome always tries to express more coding information in order to adapt to the environment during evolution.

data.problem_en: Will it be possible to cure all cancers?
data.problem_cn: 我们是否可以治愈全部癌症？

papers.title: Molecular MRI-Based Monitoring of Cancer Immunotherapy Treatment Response
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy constitutes a paradigm shift in cancer treatment. However, many patients still fail to benefit from this treatment modality. Noninvasive treatment monitoring is crucial for longitudinal tumor characterization and the early detection of non-responders.

papers.title: Targeted learning of heterogeneous treatment effect curves: immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Exploring heterogeneity in the effects of immunotherapy on survival among non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients.

data.problem_en: Is de-extinction possible?
data.problem_cn: 复活灭绝生物是否可行？

papers.title: Excess of genomic defects in a woolly mammoth on Wrangel island
papers.abstract: Woolly mammoths populated Siberia, Beringia, and North America during the Pleistocene. Using previously published mammoth sequences, we identify deletions, retrogenes, and non-functionalizing point mutations. The accumulation of detrimental mutations is consistent with genomic meltdown in response to low effective population sizes.

data.problem_en: Did ancient humans interbreed with other human-like ancestors?
data.problem_cn: 古人类是否和其他人科远古祖先发生过混血？

papers.title: The date of interbreeding between Neandertals and modern humans
papers.abstract: Comparisons of DNA sequences between Neandertals and present-day humans have shown that Neandertals share more genetic variants with non-Africans than with Africans. The last gene flow from Neandertals into Europeans likely occurred 37,000-86,000 years BP.

papers.title: Maximum likelihood evidence for Neandertal admixture in Eurasian populations from three genomes
papers.abstract: We derive the probability of mutational configurations. Our analysis allows us to formally reject a history of ancestral population structure and reveals strong support for admixture from Neandertals into Eurasian populations at 3.4-7.9%.

data.problem_en: Where do human emotions originate?
data.problem_cn: 人类情绪起源于哪里？

papers.title: Identifying the Hierarchical Emotional Areas in the Human Brain Through Information Fusion
papers.abstract: The brain basis of emotion has consistently received widespread attention. We propose to identify the hierarchical emotional areas in the human brain through multi-source information fusion and graph machine learning methods.

papers.title: Neural dynamics of emotion and cognition: from trajectories to underlying neural geometry
papers.abstract: This paper describes the outlines of a research program for understanding the cognitive-emotional brain, with an emphasis on the issue of dynamics and the interaction between emotion and cognition.

data.problem_en: Why do we stop growing?
data.problem_cn: 人类身体为什么会停止生长？

papers.title: Uncertainty and sensitivity analysis of hair growth duration in human scalp follicles
papers.abstract: Hair follicles constantly cycle through phases of growth, regression and rest. We present a mathematical model for human hair cycle with experimental data for hair growth phases, addressing the question of why hair growth terminates at certain phases.

data.problem_en: Will humans look physically different in the future?
data.problem_cn: 未来人类的外貌会变得不一样吗？

papers.title: When Autonomy Breaks: The Hidden Existential Risk of AI
papers.abstract: As AI starts to outcompete humans in various areas of life, a tipping point will be reached. We examine gradual de-skilling, where we lose skills that we currently take for granted, including critical thinking, decision-making and even social care.

data.problem_en: Why don't the orbits of planets decay and cause them to crash into each other?
data.problem_cn: 行星轨道为什么不会衰减，互相撞击？

papers.title: Orbital Decay of Short-Period Exoplanets via Tidal Resonance Locking
papers.abstract: A large fraction of known exoplanets have short orbital periods where tidal excitation of gravity waves within the host star causes the planets orbits to decay. We study the effects of tidal resonance locking.

papers.title: Doomed Worlds I: No new evidence for orbital decay in a long-term survey of 43 ultra-hot Jupiters
papers.abstract: Ultra-hot Jupiters are likely doomed by tidal forces to undergo orbital decay and eventual disruption by their stars, but the timescale is unknown. Only 1/43 planets shows detectable orbital decay.

data.problem_en: Is it possible to live permanently on another planet?
data.problem_cn: 人类可以永久在别的行星定居吗？

papers.title: Mars as an Exoplanet: Lessons from a Planet at the Edge of Habitability
papers.abstract: Mars is the Solar System canonical small, rocky planet that transitioned from early geologic activity and surface liquid water to a cold and arid planet. Understanding Mars habitability provides lessons for exoplanetary habitability.

papers.title: The Interplanetary Habitable Zone
papers.abstract: The concept of a system-wide measure of the sustainment of life for space-faring interplanetary species is introduced.

data.problem_en: Where do we put all the excess carbon dioxide?
data.problem_cn: 多余的二氧化碳我们安置到哪里？

papers.title: Optimizing carbon dioxide trapping for geological storage
papers.abstract: Carbon dioxide trapping in capillary networks of reservoir rocks is a pathway to long-term geological storage. We report how to represent a rock pore space by statistically sampled capillary networks that preserve morphological rock characteristics for CO2 storage potential prediction.

papers.title: Agent-Based Modeling for Multimodal Transportation of CO2 for Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage: CCUS-Agent
papers.abstract: An agent-based modeling tool for large-scale study of CO2 transportation flows and infrastructure in the United States. The results suggest that it is possible to capture over 9 billion tonnes of CO2 from 2025 to 2043.

data.problem_en: Can we more accurately predict extreme events such as tsunamis, hurricanes, and earthquakes?
data.problem_cn: 我们可以更准确预测海啸、飓风、地震这类极端灾害吗？

papers.title: Deep learning for magnitude prediction in earthquake early warning
papers.abstract: Fast and accurate magnitude prediction is the key to the success of earthquake early warning. We propose a new approach based on deep learning for P-wave magnitude prediction (EEWNet), which achieves excellent results in magnitude prediction.

papers.title: Real-time Bayesian inference at extreme scale: A digital twin for tsunami early warning applied to the Cascadia subduction zone
papers.abstract: We present a Bayesian inversion-based digital twin that employs acoustic pressure data from seafloor sensors to infer earthquake-induced spatiotemporal seafloor motion in real time and forecast tsunami propagation toward coastlines for early warning with quantified uncertainties.

data.problem_en: Can we create an environmentally friendly replacement for plastics?
data.problem_cn: 我们可以造出环境友好的塑料替代品吗？

papers.title: Sustainable bioplastics from amyloid fibril-biodegradable polymer blends
papers.abstract: Plastic waste production is a global challenging problem. This study proposes a simple, scalable and water-based process to produce free-standing, transparent and flexible bioplastic films by combining amyloid fibrils with biodegradable polymers. Whey is used as a model protein, sourced from dairy industry by-products, to produce sustainable, biodegradable, environmentally friendly bioplastics integrated within a circular economy.

data.problem_en: Can we achieve a situation where essentially every material can be recycled and reused?
data.problem_cn: 是否可以实现几乎全部材料循环回收再利用？

papers.title: How circular is the linear economy? Analysing circularity, resource flows and their relation to GDP
papers.abstract: The concept of Circular Economy has evolved significantly over the past decade. Through a mixed-methods analysis of global resource flows, the study demonstrates that adjusting circularity calculations for non-recoverable materials reveals a real circularity rate of 27%, far exceeding the apparent 9%. Yet even this higher rate translates to a mere 1.4% of global GDP.

papers.title: Computational Design and Co-Robotic Fabrication for Material Reuse in Architecture
papers.abstract: Material reuse offers a promising pathway by reducing raw material extraction, mitigating waste, and extending the service lifespan of carbon-sequestering materials such as timber. This paper presents an integrated framework coupling data-driven computational design with feedback-driven adaptive human-robot collaborative fabrication and assembly to enable nonstandard structures from reclaimed timber.

data.problem_en: Will we soon see the end of monocultures like wheat, maize, rice, and soy?
data.problem_cn: 小麦玉米水稻大豆这类单一农作物种植模式会终结吗？

papers.title: A Turtle Model of Food System Transformations: Embracing Citizens Diverse Values and Knowledge in Change Processes
papers.abstract: We explore the challenges and opportunities of transitioning towards sustainable food systems through democratic food governance fostering inclusive and systemic transformation. Drawing on concepts of wicked problems and systems thinking, we propose a theory of change represented as a turtle model that embraces the diversity of citizens values and knowledge to highlight multiple avenues of transformation.

data.problem_en: How can genome editing be used to treat diseases?
data.problem_cn: 基因组编辑如何用于治疗疾病？

papers.title: Gene and RNA Editing: Methods, Enabling Technologies, Applications, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Gene and RNA editing methods, technologies, and applications are emerging as innovative forms of therapy and medicine, offering more efficient implementation compared to traditional pharmaceutical treatments. Current trends emphasize the urgent need for advanced methods and technologies to detect public health threats, including diseases and viral agents. Gene and RNA editing techniques enhance the ability to identify, modify, and ameliorate the effects of genetic diseases, disorders, and disabilities.

data.problem_en: How do large biomolecules in a cell organize in an orderly yet dynamic way to efficiently carry out life activities?
data.problem_cn: 细胞内部的生物大分子，如何有序高效完成生命活动？

papers.title: Roadmap for Condensates in Cell Biology
papers.abstract: Biomolecular condensates govern essential cellular processes yet elude description by traditional equilibrium models. This roadmap clarifies key concepts: unifying terminology, outlining core physics of condensate formation, reviewing biological roles, and identifying outstanding challenges in nonequilibrium theory, multiscale simulation, and quantitative in-cell measurements.

papers.title: Determinants of Phase-Separation Propensities, Material States, and Material Properties of Biomolecular Condensates
papers.abstract: Phase separation of proteins and nucleic acids has received enormous attention due to its relevance to cellular functions. This Account puts forward theoretical frameworks for the phase-separation propensities, material states, and material properties of biomolecular condensates.

data.problem_en: How many dimensions does the universe have?
data.problem_cn: 宇宙存在多少个维度？

papers.title: Extra Dimensions Beyond the Horizon
papers.abstract: We discuss an extra-dimensional braneworld with a 5th dimension compactified on a circle. The warp factor is hyperbolic and separates the hidden and visible branes by a bulk horizon without a singularity. The two most widely separated scales of 4D physics — the 4D Planck mass and 4D cosmological constant — are determined by two physical scales in the extra dimension.

data.problem_en: Is there life elsewhere in the universe?
data.problem_cn: 宇宙中只有人类生命吗？

papers.title: The Eschatian Hypothesis
papers.abstract: The history of astronomical discovery shows that many of the most detectable phenomena are not typical members of their broader class. We propose the Eschatian Hypothesis: that the first confirmed detection of an extraterrestrial technological civilization is most likely to be an atypical example, one that is unusually loud and plausibly in a transitory, unstable, or even terminal phase.

papers.title: Constraining the Lifespan of Intelligent Technological Civilization in the Galaxy
papers.abstract: We explore constraints on the emergence and longevity of technologically intelligent civilizations in our Galaxy, considering the Fermi paradox. Our analysis suggests that if intelligent life is common, technological civilizations must be relatively short-lived, with lifetimes constrained to less than 5000 years under our most optimistic scenario.

data.problem_en: Is our Milky Way special or typical?
data.problem_cn: 我们的银河系是否特殊？

papers.title: The local galaxy distribution does not violate the cosmological principle
papers.abstract: The cosmological principle states that the Universe is statistically homogeneous and isotropic on sufficiently large scales. We show that apparent anisotropic features in the local galaxy distribution disappear when the correct comoving distance scale is used, demonstrating consistency with the cosmological principle.

papers.title: Milky Way type galaxies in a LCDM cosmology
papers.abstract: We analyse a sample of 52,000 Milky Way type galaxies from the Millennium Simulation. Our analysis suggests that the Milky Way is a typical Sb/Sc galaxy in the same mass range, formed quietly through the accretion of cold gas and small satellite systems.

data.problem_en: What is the minimum scale of space-time?
data.problem_cn: 时空最小尺度是多少？

papers.title: Spacetime with zero point length is two-dimensional at the Planck scale
papers.abstract: It is generally believed that any quantum theory of gravity should have a generic feature — a quantum of length. We provide a physical ansatz to obtain an effective non-local metric tensor such that spacetime acquires a zero-point-length of the order of the Planck length. This suggests that the physical spacetime becomes essentially 2-dimensional near Planck scale.

papers.title: Six easy roads to the Planck scale
papers.abstract: We give six arguments that the Planck scale should be viewed as a fundamental minimum or boundary for the classical concept of spacetime, beyond which quantum effects cannot be neglected and the basic nature of spacetime must be reconsidered.

data.problem_en: Is Einstein's General Relativity completely correct?
data.problem_cn: 爱因斯坦广义相对论完全正确吗？

papers.title: A Falsifiable Alternative to General Relativity
papers.abstract: Asymptotically Weyl-invariant gravity (AWIG) is developed within the Palatini formalism as a power-counting renormalizable alternative to general relativity (GR). A falsifiable prediction regarding the frequency of gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers is made. A preliminary analysis of gravitational wave GW150914 yields a maximum tension of 0.9 sigma with GR.

papers.title: Are there metric theories of gravity other than General Relativity?
papers.abstract: Current generalizations of the classical Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian formulation of General Relativity are reviewed. Some alternative variational principles are known to reproduce Einstein gravitational equations and should be regarded as equivalent descriptions of the same physical model, while other variational principles are commonly presented as truly alternative physical theories.

data.problem_en: Is water a necessary condition for life elsewhere, or is it unique to Earth?
data.problem_cn: 水是宇宙生命的必需条件，还是仅仅地球生命需要？

papers.title: Habitability and Biosignatures
papers.abstract: The search for life beyond the solar system is a central goal in exoplanetary science. Basic concepts of planetary habitability are introduced along with essential requirements for life as we know it including the requirement for liquid water, energy sources, bioessential elements, and geophysical environmental conditions conducive for life.

papers.title: Detecting Surface Liquid Water on Exoplanets
papers.abstract: Planets with large bodies of water on their surface will have more temperate and stable climates, and such planets are the ideal places for life-as-we-know-it to arise and evolve. Rotational variability in the reflectance of an exoplanet may reveal surface features rotating in and out of view, including oceans.

data.problem_en: What are the obstacles to deep space exploration?
data.problem_cn: 是什么阻碍人类开展深空探索？

papers.title: Toward the Stars: Technological, Ethical, and Sociopolitical Dimensions of Interstellar Exploration
papers.abstract: This paper explores multifaceted aspects of interstellar travel, exploring advancements in propulsion systems, habitat construction, and life support alongside ethical, sociopolitical, and philosophical questions. Key challenges include the immense energy required for propelling spacecraft across interstellar distances, radiation shielding, and developing sustainable life support systems.

papers.title: Beyond Beryllium: AI-Accelerated Materials Discovery for Interstellar Spacecraft Shielding
papers.abstract: Project Daedalus specified a 9 mm beryllium erosion shield to protect the spacecraft payload. Here we systematically screen 20 candidate materials using DFT and graph neural networks, identifying hexagonal boron nitride and boron carbide as dual-function materials offering simultaneous mechanical protection and neutron radiation shielding.

papers.title: Self-sustaining living habitats in extraterrestrial environments
papers.abstract: Standard definitions of habitability assume that life requires planetary gravity wells to stabilize liquid water and regulate surface temperature. Temperature, pressure, volatile loss, radiation levels and nutrient availability all appear to be surmountable obstacles to the survival of photosynthetic life in space or on celestial bodies with thin atmospheres.

data.problem_en: What is the volume, composition, and significance of the deep biosphere?
data.problem_cn: 深部生物圈的体积、成分，意义是什么？

papers.title: Microbes in porous environments: From active interactions to emergent feedback
papers.abstract: Microbes thrive in diverse porous environments from soil and riverbeds to human lungs and cancer tissues. The subsurface refers to area of the Earth crust and deep sea sediments estimated to be several kilometers thick. Despite extreme conditions, lack of light, oxygen, and high pressures and temperatures, they harbor active microbial communities. Although low in density and metabolism, microorganisms in the continental and oceanic subsurface account for more than half of total microbial biomass.

data.problem_en: Can xenotransplantation solve the donor organ shortage?
data.problem_cn: 异种器官移植能否解决供体器官短缺？

papers.title: Current status of xenotransplantation from an immunobiological standpoint
papers.abstract: Xenotransplantation, which involves the transplantation of organs, tissues, or cells from animals into humans, is emerging as a promising solution to mitigate the global shortage of human donor organs. Nonetheless, its clinical application is constrained by significant immunological and physiological barriers — most notably, the rapid rejection of xenografts by both the innate and adaptive immune systems. This review discusses critical immunological challenges such as natural antibodies, complement activation, coagulation dysregulation, and cellular immune responses mediated by T cells, macrophages, and natural killer cells. Advances in genetic engineering — such as the development of multi-knockout pigs that lack major xenoantigens and the transgenic expression of human regulatory proteins — have considerably prolonged xenograft survival in preclinical models. While recent breakthroughs, including pig-to-human transplants, demonstrate considerable clinical potential, challenges remain in achieving long-term graft survival.
